In [[mathematical analysis]], a '''positively''' (or '''positive''') '''invariant set''' is a [[Set (mathematics)|set]] with the following properties:

Suppose <math>\dot{x}=f(x)</math> is a [[dynamical system]], <math> x(t,x_0) </math> is a trajectory, and <math> x_0 </math> is the initial point. Let <math> \mathcal{O} := \left \lbrace x \in \mathbb{R}^n\mid \varphi (x) = 0 \right \rbrace</math> where <math>\varphi</math> is a real-valued [[Function (mathematics)|function]]. The set <math>\mathcal{O}</math> is said to be positively invariant if <math>x_0 \in \mathcal{O}</math> implies that <math>x(t,x_0) \in \mathcal{O} \ \forall \ t \ge 0 </math>

In other words, once a trajectory of the system enters <math>\mathcal{O}</math>, it will never leave it again.
